name: Fraud — account abuse / bot defence (signup floods, credential stuffing, scraping)
category: Currently-stated (README) target — fraud detection on identity/account layer
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Account abuse and bot defence (signup floods, credential stuffing, scraping)
domain_fit.one_line_definition: An identity / edge platform decides in <50 ms on every login, signup, password-reset or API call whether the traffic is human-real-user, abusive-human, or bot, using per-IP / per-fingerprint / per-route / per-(IP x user-agent) velocity features.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Block credential-stuffing waves before they hit the auth backend (detect 'many usernames against one IP/fingerprint/JA4'). 2) Throttle or challenge signup floods from a single device or ASN (detect 'many signups per device, per IP, per network'). 3) Detect content scraping (high-cardinality endpoint traversal: one fingerprint hitting many distinct URLs or product IDs). 4) Power adaptive challenges (CAPTCHA, OTP, step-up auth) based on real-time risk scores rather than static rules. 5) Feed downstream ML risk scorers (Castle, Cloudflare BM, in-house) with consistent rolling features across edge and in-app.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Wire events typically: login_attempt {ts, ip, user_agent, ja4, device_fp, account_id_hash, success, reason}, signup_attempt {ts, ip, ja4, device_fp, email_domain, route}, password_reset {ts, ip, account_id_hash}, otp_request {ts, ip, channel}, page_view / api_call {ts, ip, route, status, fp, asn, country}. Volume is dominated by login_attempt and api_call. Key dimensions are IP, JA3/JA4 TLS fingerprint, device fingerprint / visitor ID, ASN, route, account_id, and the cross product (ip x ua), (ip x route), (fp x route).
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Heavy use of beava counters + n_unique + velocity primitives in 1m / 5m / 1h / 24h sliding windows. Per-IP: count(login_attempts), count(login_failures), failure_ratio = failures / attempts, n_unique(account_id) (the credential-stuffing signal: many usernames against one host), n_unique(route) (the scraping signal: one fingerprint traversing the catalog), velocity(login_attempts). Per-fingerprint: count(signup_attempts), n_unique(ip) (proxy rotation), distribution(country). Per-route: count(login_attempts), failure_ratio, rate-of-change. Per-(IP x UA): velocity to catch homogeneous bot fleets behind the same proxy pool. Distance primitive can also drive impossible-travel on (account_id, last_known_geo).
domain_fit.entity_grain: Composite. Primary keys are IP (v4/v6), device fingerprint / visitor ID, JA4 / TLS fingerprint, route, ASN, account_id_hash, and ordered pairs (IP x UA), (IP x route), (fp x route), (account_id x ip).
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Sliding windows dominate (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 24h). Approximate aggregates (HLL for n_unique, CMS for top-k IPs/routes) are perfectly acceptable on the IP / fingerprint / route axes because cardinality is explosive and the risk score is monotonic in the count. Tumbling windows are useful only for billing / reporting. Session windows are useful for the 'burst of 200 requests then go quiet' pattern but are not strictly required if 1m and 5m sliding counters exist.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: At-least-once is acceptable — the decision is a risk score, not money. Double-counting one login attempt does not produce a regulatory or financial error; it slightly biases the velocity feature upward, which is the safe direction for fraud.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Read p99 <10 ms is the operational target for edge / inline auth gates; <50 ms end-to-end is the hard ceiling before login UX degrades. beava's sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits well inside this budget.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Single-digit seconds end-to-end, ideally <1 s. Credential-stuffing waves can ramp from 0 to hundreds of thousands of requests in seconds (Auth0 reports up to 69% of daily login attempts are stuffing on attack days), so stale features defeat detection. beava's push-on-event model with no broker hop fits this.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Steady-state: an identity provider the size of Auth0 sees ~100M logins/day (~1.2k EPS average) but credential stuffing produces bursts of hundreds of thousands of login requests in seconds — peak EPS on a single tenant routinely 10–100x average. An edge / WAF buyer (Cloudflare, Fastly, Castle) is on a different scale entirely: Cloudflare proxies billions of HTTP requests/day across its network. A single beava node at the published ~684k EPS (M4, TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) comfortably covers a single mid-size IDP or a regional shard of a bot-management vendor; a global edge buyer would need horizontal partitioning (which beava does not yet do in-process). [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly 1:1 to 2:1 reads-per-write at the auth gate (every login_attempt is one write and one batch read of 20–100 features), shifting to read-heavy on read-only API traffic where many requests are scored but only a fraction generate state-mutating writes.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Dominated by IP and fingerprint cardinality. A medium IDP / SaaS sees ~10M distinct IPs/month and ~50M distinct device fingerprints/year (rough order). At ~200 B per per-entity feature vector (a handful of counters + HLLs), that is ~10 GB live state for IPs alone, and 10–50 GB for fingerprints — fits in RAM on a single modern box, but requires aggressive TTL/eviction or beava risks OOM on IP/fp blowup during DDoS-class events. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Explosive on IP (especially with residential proxy networks rotating millions of /32s), explosive on device fingerprint / visitor ID, bounded on route (hundreds to low thousands), bounded on JA4 (low thousands of distinct fingerprints globally), slowly-growing on account_id.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Seconds to hours for hot velocity features (1m/5m/15m/1h sliding windows). 24h–7d for medium-term reputation. 30–90 d for long-term IP / fingerprint reputation feeding ML risk scorers. Most state should be evictable on TTL because the IP / fingerprint cardinality is unbounded.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 20–100+ features per login / signup decision is industry standard (per-IP velocity, per-fp velocity, per-route failure ratio, per-ASN reputation, JA4 cluster features, impossible-travel distance, plus historical aggregates). Strongly favors a batch_get path — exactly what beava ships.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Best-effort to crash-safe. Risk scores are derived state, not money. If a node loses its 5-minute sliding window during a crash, the buyer's risk model degrades for a few minutes but no regulatory or financial obligation is violated. beava's WAL + snapshot story is more than enough; some buyers would happily run beava with WAL disabled in exchange for higher throughput.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Strong fit for edge / sidecar / single-binary topologies. Buyers in this space (Castle, Fingerprint, Cloudflare Bot Management) are pushing detection logic to the edge (Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute) precisely because origin round-trips are too slow. beava's single-binary, no-broker, push-on-event model maps well to a per-region or per-PoP deployment. Multi-region active-active is desirable but not strictly required if a region can lose state for the few minutes its features are degraded. The hard limit is that beava v0 has no in-process sharding, so a single tenant that exceeds one box must be hand-sharded externally.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Platform / infrastructure / SecOps engineering teams at: (a) identity providers (Auth0/Okta, WorkOS, Stytch, Descope), (b) bot-management / fraud-prevention vendors (Castle, Fingerprint, DataDome, Kasada, Arkose, HUMAN, Cequence), (c) edge / WAF vendors (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai), and (d) large in-house platform teams at e-commerce, fintech, gaming and ticketing. Distinctly NOT the corporate 'fraud team' — this is platform / infra / SecOps, which is exactly the line beava's positioning correctly identifies.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Bot management is a $1.0–1.3B market in 2025, projected to $2.2–4.9B by 2030 at 18–24% CAGR (multiple analyst estimates). Adjacent identity-fraud market is larger and growing (Sumsub: 76% of fraud now happens post-KYC, driving spend toward continuous behavioral monitoring rather than one-shot identity verification). Vendor pricing scale: Castle starts at $200/mo for 100k requests; DataDome/Kasada/HUMAN run six- to seven-figure annual contracts at enterprise scale. Auth0 alone secures ~100M logins/day; ~26B credential-stuffing attempts/month industry-wide (Akamai). [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) Credential theft surged ~160% in 2025; ~26B credential-stuffing attempts/month; the 2025 DBIR attributes 22% of breaches to compromised credentials. 2) Sumsub's finding that 76% of fraud happens post-identity-verification is forcing IDPs and platforms to invest in continuous behavioral monitoring (not just signup-time checks). 3) PSD3 / PSR (political agreement Nov 2025, applies ~mid-2026) explicitly requires PSPs to monitor login, mandate setup, beneficiary management, device recovery — broadening SCA to events that need real-time velocity features. 4) AI-driven credential stuffing tooling makes attacks cheaper and more 'human-shaped', breaking heuristic detectors and forcing buyers to add behavioral features fast. 5) DORA (in force January 17, 2025) puts operational-resilience pressure on EU financial firms' anti-fraud stacks.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: PSD3 / PSR1 (for EU regulated payments / IDPs in financial flows), DORA (operational resilience, in force Jan 2025), GDPR / CCPA (IP and device-fingerprint storage is personal data — argues for short TTLs and aggressive hashing, which beava's in-memory + WAL TTL story actually helps with), SOC 2 (most buyers will want auditable retention and access control — beava v0's lack of TLS / auth is a hard blocker here). PCI-DSS only indirectly (when the auth flow gates a payment).
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fast — 1–3 days to a working signup-flood / credential-stuffing demo on a laptop using beava's @bv.event + @bv.table primitives plus a thin auth-gate proxy. 2–4 weeks to a production pilot at an identity provider once auth and TLS are added (the v0 gaps below). The 'impossible-travel + per-IP velocity + per-fingerprint velocity' demo is the obvious one-page README example.

competition.incumbents: Generic real-time stack: Redis (counters + Lua, plus Redis Stack with Bloom / CMS / Top-K modules) is the overwhelming default; Aerospike at very high cardinality; Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for buyers who already have Kafka and want SQL semantics; Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk / Fennel as managed online feature stores feeding XGBoost-class risk scorers. Custom in-Rust services on top of RocksDB or Sled are common at scale (Cloudflare, Fastly).
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Castle (behavioral integrity, edge + in-app, recent Cloudflare integration May 2025), Fingerprint (device intelligence, visitor IDs, 'velocity signals' product), Cloudflare Bot Management (ML + JA4 + heuristics on Cloudflare's global network), DataDome, Kasada, Arkose Labs, HUMAN (formerly PerimeterX), Akamai Bot Manager, F5 / Shape, Imperva, Netacea, Cequence, IPQS, Fraudlogix. Most of these are end-to-end products, not pure feature backends — beava would more naturally sit underneath one of these vendors (or an in-house equivalent) than replace them.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster — fits the edge / PoP / sidecar topology that this market is moving toward. 2) 50+ aggregation primitives already cover the velocity / n_unique / distribution / distance features that this domain literally lives on, without writing Lua. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get matches the inline auth-gate latency budget. 4) Apache-2.0, no open-core, no SaaS lock-in — attractive to vendors who want to embed it (Castle/Fingerprint-style) rather than depend on a competitor's managed cloud. 5) Push-on-event model (HTTP/TCP push) maps directly to how WAFs and auth gates already produce events; no broker hop. 6) The 'distances' primitive cleanly expresses impossible-travel, which is otherwise hand-rolled with Redis + Haversine.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS, no auth in v0 — disqualifying for any production deployment by an IDP / regulated buyer; effectively limits beava today to in-VPC / behind-mTLS-proxy deployments. 2) No in-process sharding — a single tenant beyond ~684k EPS or ~50 GB hot state has to hand-shard externally. 3) Refuse-on-network-FS plus in-memory-only means buyers must plan local-disk WAL and cold-start replay time; the IP-cardinality blowup during a DDoS-class event could OOM a node. 4) No triggers / 'fire when counter crosses threshold' — bot defence really wants 'fire CAPTCHA when this IP's 1-minute failure ratio crosses 0.4', and today that has to be polled. 5) No multi-tenancy primitives — a bot-management vendor serving many customers needs per-tenant isolation, quotas, and rate-limit accounting that beava doesn't ship. 6) No secondary indexes / no 'list all IPs with failure_ratio > x' query — limits the SOC / analyst surface.
competition.integration_surface: Producers: WAF / reverse proxy (Nginx, Envoy, Caddy, Cloudflare Worker, Fastly Compute) emitting events on every request; auth service / IDP emitting login_attempt / signup / reset; mobile / web SDK pushing device-fp + behavior events directly. beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits the WAF / Worker producer; TCP+msgpack :8081 fits high-throughput auth services. Consumers: rules engines (Castle scoring rules, in-house Drools / FEEL), ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM / ONNX served from a separate process pulling features via batch_get), and inline allow/deny/challenge logic in the proxy.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Buyers commonly run a deterministic rules layer (per-IP failure ratio > X, per-fingerprint signups > Y per hour) AND an ML scorer (XGBoost / LightGBM / deep model) consuming the same beava features. beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from the scorer; this is its natural seam.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public users of beava on this use case yet. [uncertain] Comparable production systems: Castle (behavioral integrity, public Cloudflare integration May 2025), Fingerprint (Velocity Signals product, public docs), Cloudflare Bot Management (multiple public blogs on JA4 + inter-request signals), Akamai (cites ~193B annual credential-stuffing attempts), Auth0 (public: ~69% of daily logins suspected stuffing on attack days). Redis publishes its 'fraud-detection brain' case studies for banks. RisingWave has a public blog 'Real-Time Features for Account Takeover Detection'.
adoption_signals.community_discussions: No beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion threads located on this topic yet. [uncertain] Broader community is very active: OWASP credential-stuffing prevention cheat sheet, Cloudflare blog on JA4 + inter-request signals, Castle's 'Roll your own bot detection' series, Hacker News threads on Castle for Cloudflare (May 2025), Reddit r/sysadmin and r/netsec threads on residential-proxy credential-stuffing waves.
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: Generic fraud demo present at /tmp/docker-desktop-root/run/desktop/mnt/host/d/Code/Beava/beava/python/beava/demos/fraud (events.jsonl + schema.json). No dedicated bot-defence / credential-stuffing / signup-flood demo identified in the repository as of the snapshot reviewed. [uncertain]
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Maximum. This is an actively adversarial domain — attackers retool weekly (AI-driven stuffing tooling, residential-proxy pools, JA4-spoofing toolkits, headless-browser polymorphism). Feature drift is fast; the buyer expects to add and retire features continuously, which argues for a developer-ergonomic feature backend (beava's @bv.event / @bv.table model) rather than a SQL-on-Flink pipeline.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Long historical lookback / batch backfill — beava is in-memory only, not the place to store a 90-day event log for retrospective model training (that belongs in Parquet / a lakehouse). 2) Cross-entity joins ('show me all account_ids that share a device_fp with this IP cluster') — beava has no join engine; that's a graph-DB / OLAP problem. 3) Full event archive / forensic replay — WAL is for crash recovery, not for analyst-driven exploration. 4) Acting as the rules engine or the ML scorer — beava is the feature backend, not the scoring engine. 5) Acting as the WAF itself — it sits behind one. 6) Heavy state with regulator-grade durability (AML-style) — beava could do it, but the buyer in this domain doesn't need it and the technical fit is better elsewhere.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for this domain, roughly in priority order: 1) TLS termination and mutual TLS on :8081 / :8090, plus an auth model (token, mTLS, or both) on the admin / push surfaces — without this, no regulated IDP or bot-management vendor can deploy it externally. 2) In-process or sidecar sharding by key prefix, so a single tenant beyond ~684k EPS can scale within one cluster without external hand-sharding. 3) Triggers / 'callback when counter crosses threshold' — bot defence is inherently event-driven (fire CAPTCHA when fail-ratio > X), and polling 20–100 features per request just to threshold them wastes round-trips. 4) HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K approximate primitives as first-class aggregations to keep IP and fingerprint cardinality in bounded RAM; if these are already in the 50+ primitives, document them prominently for this domain. 5) Per-key TTL / sliding-window eviction so explosive IP cardinality during DDoS events doesn't OOM the box. 6) Multi-tenancy: per-tenant namespaces, quotas, and per-tenant rate-limit accounting for vendors serving many customers. 7) A streaming admin / debug surface to let SOC analysts query 'top-k IPs by failure_ratio in the last 5 minutes' without materializing the whole keyspace. 8) Hooks for residential-proxy / ASN / JA4 enrichment (either as in-process modules or as a documented producer pattern). 9) Cold-start strategy: WAL replay time on a node with tens of GB of hot IP/fp state needs to be benchmarked and bounded; otherwise a node restart becomes an outage during an active attack. 10) Authenticated PII-handling story for the GDPR / CCPA buyer (hash IPs at rest, short TTL by default, document the model).
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — this domain genuinely needs an event-driven trigger primitive ('when (ip x route).failure_ratio crosses 0.4 in the last 60 s, fire'), not only feature serving. Polling 20–100 features per request to threshold them is workable for the inline auth gate (the read is happening anyway) but is wasteful for the asynchronous 'spawn CAPTCHA / send to SOC / quarantine session' path. This is one of the most-cited gaps for the domain.
